35 The diagram shows a circuit with a battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 60 V and negligible
internal resistance, a 20 k resistor, a thermistor and a voltmeter. The resistance of the
thermistor is 20 k.
V
60 V
The temperature of the thermistor decreases, and this causes its resistance to change by 50%.
After this change, what is the reading on the voltmeter?
A
20 V
B
24 V
C
36 V
D
40 V

hints: Notice the voltmeter is connected across only the upper $20\text{ k}\Omega$ fixed resistor, while the thermistor is the lower part of the $60\text{ V}$ series loop.
Recall how an NTC thermistor behaves on cooling: its resistance increases, so a 50% change from $20\text{ k}\Omega$ means $30\text{ k}\Omega$, not $10\text{ k}\Omega$.
Use the potential divider ratio for the upper resistor: $V = 60\text{ V} \times 20/(20+30)$ and check the unit is $\text{V}$.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: the $20\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor and thermistor are in series across the $60\text{ V}$ battery, and the voltmeter is in parallel with the $20\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor only.
Decide the new thermistor resistance: cooling increases the resistance of an NTC thermistor, so a 50% increase on $20\text{ k}\Omega$ gives $R = 20\text{ k}\Omega \times 1.5 = 30\text{ k}\Omega$.
State the divider rule: in series the $60\text{ V}$ is shared in proportion to resistance, so $V_{20} = E \times R_{fixed}/(R_{fixed}+R_{thermistor})$.
Substitute values with units: $V = 60\text{ V} \times 20\text{ k}\Omega/(20\text{ k}\Omega + 30\text{ k}\Omega) = 60\text{ V} \times 20/50$.
Calculate and check: $V = 60\text{ V} \times 0.4 = 24\text{ V}$, which is less than the original $30\text{ V}$ because the lower resistance grew. This is option B.

A.explanation: Too low for the $20\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor when the total is $50\text{ k}\Omega$; it ignores the correct $20/50$ sharing of $60\text{ V}$.

B.explanation: The voltmeter reads the p.d. across the $20\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor after the thermistor becomes $30\text{ k}\Omega$, giving $60 \times 20/50 = 24\text{ V}$.

C.explanation: This is the p.d. across the $30\text{ k}\Omega$ thermistor, not across the $20\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor measured by the voltmeter.

D.explanation: This would be the reading if the thermistor resistance decreased to $10\text{ k}\Omega$; cooling an NTC thermistor increases its resistance.
